overview: White gives the f-pawn and develops the bishop to c4 at once, eyeing f7 and keeping the option of castling by hand if Black checks on h4. Black's best answers are ...Nf6 (Cozio/Bogoljubow with 4.Nc3 or 4.e5), ...Nc6 or ...Qh4+ 4.Kf1, and Black may keep the pawn but must avoid being swept off the board. Play is open, tactical and concrete.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Bc4, Nc3, Nf3 and d4 to regain f4 and attack f7.
Use the open f-file after castling or Kf1 and lines against Black's king.

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...Nf6, ...d5 or ...Nc6 to hit the centre and return the pawn on good terms.
Hold the f4 pawn with ...g5 and ...Bg7 and try to survive the initiative.

typical_structures.structure: Open game with White missing the f-pawn, king exposed on e1 or f1.

character.notes: Open and tactical from the start; both kings can be attacked and a slip loses quickly. Judged from 3...Nf6 and 3...Nc6.

gambit.notes: Black can keep the f4 pawn if they defend accurately.

soundness.notes: Objectively slightly worse for White at the top level but a sensible practical gambit; not refuted.

structure.notes: Open lines, central pawns exchanged early.

approach.notes: A recognised gambit; strong players use it occasionally.

level.notes: Needs concrete theory in the Cozio and Qh4+ lines and tactical judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3...Qh4+ 4.Kf1
sublines_that_differ.how: White loses castling but gains time against the queen.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3...g5
sublines_that_differ.how: Anderssen Defence, Black defends the pawn at once.

character.reason: Open, forcing play with both kings exposed.

gambit.reason: White gives the f-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Not refuted; a playable if slightly risky gambit.

structure.reason: Pieces play on open files and diagonals straight away.

approach.reason: Less common than the Knight's Gambit but a real line for strong players.

level.reason: Needs tactics and some theory; not obviously advanced.

plans.reason: White compensates the pawn with piece play against f7.
